**Short answer:** The counts don't show suicide prevention growing as an OIG theme. They fall from 2024 to 2025, but that drop is probably not a real decline in attention.

**Counts** (reports with at least one recommendation containing the word "suicide"; data as of 2026-11-04, 13 days old, not stale):

| Year published | Reports | Recommendations |
|---|---|---|
| 2024 | 56 | 98 |
| 2025 | 11 | 19 |

Of the 2024 recommendations, all 98 are closed as implemented. Of the 2025 recommendations, 13 are closed as implemented and 6 are still open.

**What the counts can show**
- Reports with a suicide-related recommendation were about five times more common in 2024 than in 2025.
- Suicide-related recommendations are mostly being implemented. The median time to close was about 232 days for 2024 recommendations and 242 days for 2025 recommendations.

**What they cannot show**
- **Cause of the drop.** A fall in the count could mean OIG shifted its attention. It could also mean inspection protocols changed, fewer reports were published, or the reports contain fewer recommendations. I did not check any of these. The data can't tell them apart.
- **Closure times for 2025.** The 2025 recommendations are newer and 6 are still open. Their median closure time covers only the ones already closed, so it is probably too short.
- **Keyword matching.** The count only includes recommendations whose text contains "suicide." It misses suicide-prevention work worded differently, such as "mental health" or "lethal means." It also includes recommendations that mention suicide in passing. I did not compare it with OIG's "Suicide Prevention" topic tag, which covers only about a quarter of reports.
- **Share of all reports.** I did not calculate suicide reports as a share of all reports with recommendations in each year. That share is the fairer measure of theme growth.
- **Causes and quality.** The counts say nothing about why OIG issued these recommendations or whether suicide prevention at VA is improving.

If you want, I can run the share-of-all-reports comparison, or check the "Suicide Prevention" topic tag by year.

Sources: OIG data dashboard (https://www.vaoig.gov/reports/data-dashboard) and the recommendations list (https://www.vaoig.gov/recommendations-all).

**The median for VBA recommendations is 179 days.** The data is as of 2026-11-04 and isn't stale.

**What it measures:** the median time from a report's publication to the date OIG recorded the recommendation as closed. It covers VBA recommendations that have closed. The sample is 914 of 923 closed VBA recommendations, with 966 in total and 43 still open.

- **Typical range:** the middle half of closures took 134 to 312.5 days (the quartiles).
- **Same-day closures:** 110 recommendations were closed on the day the report was published. They are probably fixed before publication, and they are included in the median.
- **Closure outcomes:** 897 closed as implemented and 26 as not implemented (2.8%).
- **Still open:** the median age of the 43 open items is 161 days. 17 are over a year old, and the oldest is 1,567 days.

**Caveats:**
- The closure date appears to record when OIG closed the item after reviewing evidence. That can come months after VBA actually did the work, so 179 days is not how long implementation took.
- The data can't show whether target dates were met. A target date is the facility's own estimate, so a later closure doesn't show a missed commitment.
- About 6% of closed recommendations across the dataset have no closure date on OIG's site, mostly from 2013 to 2016. Those are left out of the day statistics.
- Some recommendations name two offices and count for both, so group sizes can add up to more than the total.
